[MUQATIL:83:1-5/r2] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | reports | A report about the pre-Islamic market says buyers received extra measure while sellers gave short measure, using two measures and two scales and shifting between them.
[MUQATIL:83:1-5/r5] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | He glosses their loss when measuring or weighing for others as giving them less than their due.
[FARRA:v3p245#2/r3] FARRA, d. 207 · author | holds | In كالوهم/وزنوهم the suffix is an accusative object with a benefactive sense, equivalent to measured for them; a Hijazi Bedouin woman's usage confirms it.
[MAJAZ:v1p14/r8] MAJAZ, d. 209 · author | holds | The lām is understood but omitted in كالوهم and وزنوهم: ‘when they measure or weigh for them.’
[MAJAZ:v2p289/r2] MAJAZ, d. 209 · author | holds | كالوهم and وزنوهم mean measured or weighed for them; Khuffāf's poetry witnesses the construction.
[MAJAZ:v2p289/r3] MAJAZ, d. 209 · خفاف | reports | Khuffāf's verse is cited as evidence for the object suffix in the meaning “for them.”
[AKHFASH:v2p572/r1] AKHFASH, d. 215 · author | holds | كالوهم وزنوهم means measuring or weighing people; Hijazi usage says كِلْت زيدا and وزنتُه for doing so on his behalf.
[IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p519#3/r1] IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB, d. 276 · author | holds | كالوهم and وزنوهم mean they measured or weighed for them; Arabic uses the recipient suffix directly where لك is meant.
[IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p519#3/r2] IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB, d. 276 · author | holds | يخسرون means they shortchange people.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r10] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · لبيد | reports | Labīd’s line means the sun began to set; the sun is unstated and كافر evokes the covering darkness.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r11] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · طرفة | reports | In Ṭarafa’s line, منها refers to the omitted wasteland: “I wish I could ransom you from the desert.”
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r12] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farrāʾ explains the omitted complement as السفه: the fool runs toward folly when restrained.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r14] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · المثقب العبدي | reports | Al-Farrāʾ cites al-Muthaqib al-ʿAbdī, who alludes to evil alongside good before explicitly naming evil in the next line.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r15] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · author | holds | In كالواهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون, the omitted preposition ل is restored: they measure or weigh goods for other people.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r8] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · حميد بن ثور | reports | Ḥumayd ibn Thawr’s poem leaves its referent implicit: وصهباء منها means a tawny she-camel among camels.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p143/r9] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · حاتم | reports | Ḥātim’s line uses بها with an omitted referent, the soul: “when the soul rattles.”
[TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Al-Ṭabarī describes wayl as a valley of Hell’s pus for those who shortchange people in measures and weights, withholding their due full amount; mutaffif comes from something slight or scant.
[TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · عكرمة | reports | ʿIkrima swears that every measurer and weigher is in the Fire: none gives the same measure or weight that they themselves demand. | mentions 83:1
[TAB-FULL:v24p186/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | When they measure or weigh for others, they shortchange them.
[TAB-FULL:v24p186/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | In Hijazi usage, expressions like weighing someone their due or measuring their food mean weighing or measuring it for that person.
[TAB-FULL:v24p186/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · عيسى بن عمر | reports | ʿĪsā b. ʿUmar parses hum as a separate nominative subject, pauses after the verbs, and reads the sense as They shortchange.
[TAB-FULL:v24p186/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | prefers | Al-Ṭabarī prefers attaching hum to the verbs as their object: the spelling without a separating alif shows it is a connected object pronoun, not a new subject.
[ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r10] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | On the preferred parse, the pronoun in kālūhum is an object meaning 'they measured for them'; it must be joined to the verb, so one cannot pause after kālū.
[ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r11] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | reports | Some treat hum as emphasis for the subject pronoun in kālū, which would permit pausing after the verb.
[ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r12] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | prefers | He prefers parsing hum as an accusative object meaning 'for them'; if it were emphasis, the written text would contain an alif before hum.
[ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r8] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | When they measure or weigh for other people, they reduce the amount given.
[ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r9] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | Arabic permits the form yukh'sirūn here, although he knows of no one who recited that form in this place.
[NAHHAS:v5p173/r10] NAHHAS, d. 338 · عيسى بن عمر | reports | Isa ibn Umar’s pause places a stop after كالوا, then begins the subject هم before أو وزنوا.
[NAHHAS:v5p173/r11] NAHHAS, d. 338 · غيره | reports | Another analysis treats هم as an emphatic pronoun, as in قاموا هم.
[NAHHAS:v5p173/r12] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | prefers | Nahhas prefers accusative: the written form lacks an alif, and the sequence requires وإذا كالوا لهم, with the preposition لام omitted.
[NAHHAS:v5p173/r13] NAHHAS, d. 338 · أبو زيد | reports | Abu Zayd’s verse جنيتك أكموءا وعساقلا illustrates deleting a preposition with a verb taking a direct and a prepositional object.
[NAHHAS:v5p173/r14] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | Other cited poetry illustrates omitted prepositions with two-object verbs, including أمرتك الخير, نبيت عبد الله, and أستغفر الله ذنبا; the poets are unnamed here.
[NAHHAS:v5p173/r8] NAHHAS, d. 338 · أبو عمرو بن العلاء | reports | Most grammarians, including Abu Amr ibn al-Ala, al-Kisaʾi, and al-Akhfash, parse the attached pronouns as accusative objects, following Sibawayh’s analogy with كَلْتُكَ and صَدْتُكَ.
[NAHHAS:v5p173/r9] NAHHAS, d. 338 · عيسى بن عمر | reports | Isa ibn Umar parses the pronouns as nominative: they themselves make the measure or weight deficient, beginning a new clause after كالوا.
[THALABI:v10p149#3/r4] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The phrase means when they measure or weigh for people; Arabic can say I measured or weighed you to mean I did so for you.
[THALABI:v10p149#3/r5] THALABI, d. 427 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farraʾ says using the direct object in this construction is a dialect of the people of the Hijaz and neighboring regions.
[THALABI:v10p149#3/r6] THALABI, d. 427 · عيسى بن عمر | reports | Isa ibn Umar parses the verbs as two separate words, pausing after measured or weighed and beginning a new clause with they shortchange.
[THALABI:v10p149#3/r7] THALABI, d. 427 · حمزة | reports | Abu Ubayd thinks Hamza may likewise have read the verbs as separate words.
[THALABI:v10p149#3/r8] THALABI, d. 427 · أبو عبيد | prefers | Abu Ubayd prefers joining each verb to its object, citing the written form without an alif and idiomatic Arabic transitive usage.
[THALABI:v10p149#3/r9] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | Yukhsirūn means they reduce or shortchange.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r12] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | The second verb omits لهم because the intended sense, measuring or weighing for them, is clear; the cheater gives them less than due.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farrāʾ says this transitive construction is characteristic of speakers in the Hijaz and neighboring areas.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · أبو عبيدة | reports | Abū ʿUbayda cites a line about hunting deliberately as an example for an object that means doing it for someone.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الكسائي | reports | Al-Kisāʾī says the object pronoun is accusative in expressions such as weigh or measure me this much.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الفراء والزجاج | prefers | Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj say not to pause after kālū: the pronoun is attached as in they struck them; al-Zajjāj rejects treating it as emphasis because the written text would then have an alif before it.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310#2/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · المفسرون | reports | The commentators say the short-measurers reduce what they sell or weigh for others, as in the prohibition against reducing the balance. | mentions 55:9
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p310/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The phrasing means they measure or weigh for other people; Arabic can say either that they measured someone the food or measured the food for him.
[JISHUMI:v10p7317/r10] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Related usage describes an underfilled vessel and says all descendants of Adam are close to a full measure.
[JISHUMI:v10p7317/r11] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | No one has superiority over another except through piety.
[JISHUMI:v10p7317/r5] JISHUMI, d. 494 · عامة القراء | reports | The common reading joins “they measure for them” as a transitive construction, with “them” as the object; ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar instead pauses after “they measure” and starts “they are defrauders” with “they” as subject, a reading attributed to Ḥamzah.
[JISHUMI:v10p7317/r6] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | prefers | The author prefers the joined reading because the written form lacks an alif, Arabic says “I measured your due” meaning “for you,” and the readers unanimously use it.
[JISHUMI:v10p7317/r7] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Ṭafīf means tiny or insignificant; a mutaffif reduces another person's proper measure or weight, whether by a small shortfall or a subtle theft.
[JISHUMI:v10p7317/r8] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | reports | One explanation names the act for the tiny amount missing from the rightful measure.
[JISHUMI:v10p7317/r9] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | reports | Another view calls the act a secret theft of a small amount.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r3] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | When measuring or weighing for others, they give less; Arabic may direct

ly say I measured or weighed you, just as it may say I did these things for you.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r4] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · أبو عبيدة | reports | Abu Ubayda says Isa ibn Umar parses the verbs and hum as separate words, pausing after kalu or wazanu; Abu Ubayda prefers the unified reading.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r5] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · أبو عبيدة | prefers | Abu Ubayda prefers reading each verb with its object as one word: the manuscripts omit the alif that separated forms would require, and Arabic permits the direct construction kalatuka and wazantuka.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r6] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | Yukhsirun means they reduce or shortchange.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p362/r7] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · نافع | reports | Nafi says Ibn Umar warned merchants to fear God and give full measure and weight, because short-measurers stand at Resurrection sweating to halfway up their ears.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r14] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | In kaluhum and wazanuhum, the pronoun refers to people as direct objects, with the preposition removed and the verb made transitive; cited poetry likewise uses the verb for someone.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r1] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | reports | Alternatively, the pronoun stands for the omitted measured or weighed amount, with the genitive noun taking its place.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r10] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · الفضيل | reports | Al-Fudayl says shortchanging the scale blackens one's face on the Day of Resurrection.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r11] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · عبد الملك بن مروان | reports | A Bedouin rebuked Abd al-Malik: if cheaters face this threat, what of a ruler taking Muslims' property without measuring it?
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r2] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | rejects | He rejects making the pronoun the subject referring to the cheaters: that reverses the point from how they treat recipients to who performs the act, producing incoherent discourse.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r3] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | rejects | He also rejects relying on the mushaf's omission of the alif after plural waw to rule out the subject reading; orthography is not consistently conventional and the alif is not pronounced or meaningful.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r4] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | The alif after plural waw merely distinguishes it visually from a singular verb, and some scribes omit it because context already distinguishes the forms.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r5] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · عيسى بن عمر، حمزة | reports | Isa ibn Umar and Hamza do read the pronouns as referring to the cheaters, pausing at both waw letters to make their reading clear.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r6] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | They likely buy only by measure, since it lets them steal by manipulating how full the measure is; when giving, either measure or weight lets them shortchange.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p720/r7] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | Yukhsirun means they diminish the amount; one says a scale loses or causes a loss.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r10] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · عيسى بن عمر | reports | Isa ibn ʿUmar separates the verbs and pauses after each: sellers shortchange when they themselves weigh or measure; Hamza transmits this reading, with هم reinforcing the pronoun.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r12] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | يخسرون is a causative form, both خسر and أخسر can mean to reduce or spoil, and the object of كالوهم is omitted.
[TABRISI:83:1-3/r17] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | When measuring or weighing for others, they short them; the language allows either a direct object or “for them.”
[TABRISI:83:1-3/r18] TABRISI, d. 548 · ابن مسعود | reports | Ibn Masʿūd compares prayer to a measure: whoever fills it is repaid fully by God, while the warning against defrauding is familiar.
[TABRISI:83:1-3/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · عيسى بن عمر | reports | ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar reads the pronoun in “they measure them” as an independent word in nominative position or as emphasis on the subject pronoun.
[TABRISI:83:1-3/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | prefers | The other readers' object-pronoun analysis is correct: they measure or weigh for their customers.
[TABRISI:83:1-3/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The Hijaz dialect says “I weighed you your due” or “measured your food,” matching the Qurʾanic construction; other dialects add “for you.”
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52#2/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | “When they measure or weigh for them,” the defrauders reduce the amount; on this parsing, “hum” is the object and one should not pause after “measured.”
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52#2/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · بعض الناس | reports | An alternative takes “hum” as an emphatic pronoun, allowing a pause after “measured.”
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52#2/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | prefers | The author prefers the first grammatical analysis, where “hum” is the object pronoun and one does not pause after “measured.”
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p52#2/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · امرأة أعرابية | reports | Al-Farrāʾ cites a Bedouin woman’s line as evidence for the idiom of measuring out to someone, including the form “kīl lanā.”
[RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | One parses “they measured them” as “they measured for them,” deleting the preposition and making the verb transitive; al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ cite Hijazi usage.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | A second parse omits a noun and puts its genitive pronoun in its place: they measured or weighed what was due to them.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · عيسى بن عمر وحمزة | reports | ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Ḥamzah read the pronouns as emphatic objects attached to the verbs, with a pause at the two wāws.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الفراء والزجاج | rejects | Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj reject that reading because the written form lacks the expected alif; al-Kashshāf objects that Qurʾānic orthography is not always conventional, but Rāzī says the early spelling practice should have been preserved.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjāj says akhsara al-mīzān and khasara al-mīzān both mean to diminish the balance; al-Muʾarrij says “they diminish” is Qurayshi usage.
[QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عباس | reports | A Prophetic warning pairs five wrongs with consequences: broken covenants bring enemies, rejecting God's law poverty, immorality plague, short measure drought, and withholding alms the loss of rain.
[QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | Al-Bazzar transmits the warning by gist, and Malik also relates it from Ibn ʿUmar.
[QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مالك بن دينار | reports | Malik ibn Dinar tells of a dying neighbor who used two measures and saw them grow into mountains of fire when struck together.
[QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · عكرمة | reports | ʿIkrimah swears every measurer or weigher is destined for Hell, even when asked whether this applies to his son.
[QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الأصمعي | reports | Al-Asmaʿi quotes a Bedouin saying manliness cannot reside in measure rims or scale tongues; it is also related from ʿAli.
[QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · عبد خير | reports | ʿAbd Khayr says ʿAli overturned a scale that gave excess saffron, ordering accurate weight first and voluntary excess afterward.
[QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · نافع | reports | Nafiʿ says Ibn ʿUmar warned short-measurers will stand in sweat up to half their ears.
[QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو هريرة | reports | Abu Hurayrah says Medina's deputy recited this surah at dawn; he prayed against a trader who bought with full measure but sold short.
[QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | rejects | The alternative nominative reading is rejected because the first verb would have no predicate.
[QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r10] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Yakhsirun means to reduce or make the measure come up short.
[QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الأخفش والفراء | reports | Al-Akhfash and al-Farra read “measure or weigh them” as “measure or weigh for them,” with the preposition omitted.
[QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farra cites a Hijazi woman's wording to illustrate the verb: a merchant measures two units for us.
[QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الزجاج والكسائي | reports | Al-Zajjaj and al-Kisaʾi require joining the attached hum pronoun to the verb rather than pausing after kalu or wazanu.
[QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو عبيد | reports | Abu ʿUbayd says ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar treated hum as a separate emphatic word and paused; he thinks Hamzah may have read likewise.
[QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو عبيد | prefers | Abu ʿUbayd prefers treating verbs and pronoun as one word because of the spelling and Arabic transitive usage.
[QURTUBI-FULL:83:2-3/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | On the common reading, hum is an accusative object referring to people, either with an omitted preposition or omitted noun.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:83:3-6/r1] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | When they measure or weigh for people, the preposition is omitted and the verb made transitive, as supported by the cited poetry.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:83:3-6/r2] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | Alternatively, the omitted object is their measured amount; treating the separate pronoun as emphasis for the attached pronoun disrupts the contrast of taking and giving and conflicts with Qur'anic spelling.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p323/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The object pronoun refers to people; the phrasing means they measure or weigh for them, omitting the preposition and making the verb transitive.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p323/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | reports | They may measure incoming goods because measuring le

ts them exploit the filling and steal, while weighing allows similar manipulation; when giving out goods they use both measures.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p323/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Yukhsirūn means they reduce what they give; one says that a scale has lost weight or that someone has made it short.
[QASHANI:83:1-5/r1] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | Beyond literal cheating in measures, the verses concern cheating on the true scale of justice, where character and deeds are measured.
[QASHANI:83:1-5/r3] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | They undervalue others' virtues through arrogance and love of superiority; Qashani links this to 3:188. | mentions 3:188
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p424/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Taffif is reduction, from something tiny and insignificant; a mutaffif cheats by an inconspicuous small amount in weight or measure.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | When they measure for others, they collect what is due to themselves; when they measure or weigh for others, they make the recipients take less.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · السدي | reports | He says it was revealed in Medina about a man called Abu Juhayna who owned two measures, took with the full one and gave with the short one; it is also said to be the first surah revealed there.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عباس | reports | He says the warning against short measure was revealed in Medina, where the practice was especially corrupt, and the surah corrected people; another account places revelation between Mecca and Medina to reform them before the Prophet arrived.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The prior surah discussed the blessed, the wretched, and the great Day of Judgment; this surah turns to a particularly contemptible sin, cheating in measure for negligible gain.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Measure and weigh normally take their recipient with لام, which can be omitted so the suffix pronoun becomes a direct object; the measured commodity itself is omitted.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · عيسى، حمزة | reports | They treat the object as omitted and هم as a nominative pronoun reinforcing the subject wāw.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p426/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزمخشري | reports | He rejects taking هم as a subject pronoun, arguing it would make the sentence about who personally does the weighing rather than the action of cheating.
